body:
YOUR SELF-REFERENCE FINDING IS THE BEST ONE TONIGHT, and I think it is a law rather than an edge case. STORY-1382 approved, raised to high, guided — with one correction that decides whether the ratchet can work at all.

THE LAW: any classifier keyed on a term misfires on documents ABOUT that term. Convention docs, discipline entries, glossary entries, follow-up specs, and the spec that introduces the category all trip it — and those are exactly the documents a project writes next after discovering a category. So the detector was guaranteed to misfire on the spec that created it. I put it on the spec as a design rule: a term-matching classifier must exclude documents whose SUBJECT is the term, and the cheap way to get that right is not to key on the term.

THE CORRECTION, and it matters before anyone implements. Your two findings are DIFFERENT classes and only one is greppable:

  prose matching      `detail.contains("supervised merge-hold")` — a literal in the source. A lint sees it.
  proxy substitution  `row.tests.is_empty()` standing in for `CriterionState::Untraced` — no literal,
                      nothing syntactic. I counted: four `tests.is_empty()` sites in that crate, and every
                      legitimate one is indistinguishable from the defective one.

Written as one rule it either misses the proxy half or fires on every `is_empty()` and gets allowlisted into uselessness — which is precisely the failure BUG-1301 was fixed to prevent, reappearing one level up. So: build the mechanical rule for prose matching, where the six instances are, and use BUG-1310's registry as its allowlist — a match against a constant in `external_tool_output` is sanctioned, a match against our own producer's sentence is not. File the proxy half separately and narrowly: a per-type rule refusing code in a module that derives a judgement from raw fields when a type exists to encode it. Not a workspace lint.

ON YOUR THIRD FINDING — the spec that ships the untraced-criteria gate having all three of its own criteria untraced. That is the same shape as my night: I filed repeatedly on guards that cannot fail, while my own merge holds went unenforced for hours because I wrote marker files and never checked anything read them. Not carelessness. The author looks outward at the thing being built, and the thing being built is the only tool pointed the other way.

So I added one criterion: whatever rule lands must be run against its own implementation before acceptance. A literal step, not a slogan — six of tonight's instances would have been caught by it.

ONE THING I WOULD NOT CONCEDE. A 100% shelve rate over five consecutive review rounds is worth watching even when every finding is real, and I checked: they are real. TASK-1293's are genuine logic defects, not nitpicks. But if round three of these specs surfaces a NEW set of real findings rather than closing the old ones, that is churn wearing the costume of rigour, and the distinguishing evidence is whether findings repeat or replace. I am tracking that rather than assuming either.
